MAJOR: last_reviewed_HEAD derivation is contractually vague: invariants define first-vs-subsequent review, and 'no shared last_reviewed_head pointer', but not how the delta base is derived (presumably latest evidence head per item). Unspecified behavior when the stored head is not an ancestor of HEAD (rebase/force-push) or prior evidence is corrupt/unreadable → ambiguous fail-closed vs full-review fallback. Add explicit invariant + failure-matrix cases (EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE, DELTA_BASE_DIVERGED).

empty_delta_rule trusts path+header/schema classification of excluded files; a static header or valid-JSON payload under engineering/** or data/backlog/** can hide review-relevant content from the delta diff. Schema checks must be semantic (required keys, record shape, size bounds), and any executable content under excluded paths should be a hard fail, not just 'malformed' fail.

Concurrency control is declarative only ('single writer per AGENTS; concurrent sessions forbidden') with no enforcement (no lockfile/PID guard). Two sessions sharing a working tree can interleave worktree+untracked encoding scans and evidence writes, silently producing wrong candidate keys.

Generated engineering/design/<ID>.md has no drift gate: item.design_pack (source of truth) and the committed generated MD can diverge after edits; rollback assumes the MDs are deletable but CI never proves regenerated output matches committed content. Add a render-and-compare check in Gate 1/precheck.
MINOR: Encoding gate exclusion list is path-based, unlike the content-verified empty_delta_rule — inconsistent trust model; reuse excluded_content_check for encoding exclusions too.
failure_matrix lacks design-pack version-mismatch case (item pack version 1 during enforce_from migration vs config required version 2) and encoding-gate case for unreadable/binary files.
'T2/T3 require 1.5/1/2.5/2' is opaque shorthand; spell out the gate mapping (Gate 1, Gate 1.5, Gate 2.5, Gate 2) to avoid gate-selection drift.
Redaction says 'reason text is redacted' while delta re-review reason feeds the prompt/evidence — state explicitly what the prompt sees vs what is persisted to avoid contradictory contracts.
Observability is stderr/exit only; emit one machine-readable JSON gate result per run for the trail (cheap, enables final-report metrics already promised).
NIT: Encoding scan of committed base..HEAD duplicates worktree scan for files unchanged in the worktree; scope to index+worktree+untracked plus deleted-skip for perf.

'One 1.5/2.5 per candidate' plus head-scoped candidate keys means data-noise commits still mint candidates; the empty-diff rule mitigates, but consider deduping candidates with empty review-relevant diff entirely.
SUMMARY: Sound design overall: delta binding, evidence integrity via excluded_content_check, explicit guardrails/CL mapping, and revert-only rollback are enterprise-appropriate for tooling.
Top risks: unspecified delta-base derivation under rebase/corrupt evidence, spoofable path/header-based exclusions, unenforced single-writer assumption, and generated design-doc drift.
All are addressable with added invariants, failure-matrix cases, and a render-and-compare gate without scope expansion.
